chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz said:

I asked Isma'il ibn Ja'far: When is the testimony of a boy permitted? He said: When he reaches ten years of age. I said: Does his matter (affairs) become valid? He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) took Aisha (peace be upon her) while she was ten years old, and a girl is not taken (for marriage) until she becomes a woman. So when a boy has ten years, his matter is valid and his testimony is valid.
ai.seo_question: At what age is a boy's testimony considered valid in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Isma'il ibn Ja'far establishes ten years as the age of legal competence (bulugh) for boys regarding testimony, drawing a parallel to the Prophet's marriage to Aisha. It clarifies that while marriage requires full maturity, the capacity for testimony is granted at ten, reflecting the Shia juristic distinction between general legal capacity and full marital readiness. This hadith is foundational in the chapter of evidences (Bayinat) for determining the validity of witnesses in judicial matters.
